breaking.headline: Futures point to sharp rebound after brutal week
breaking.fact: Nasdaq-100 futures jumped about 3.1–3.6% and S&P 500 futures about 2.4–2.9% Monday morning after the S&P 500's seventh straight loss and Friday's 3.7% drop put it in correction; Capital Economics' Jonas Goltermann called the move a likely 'dead cat bounce' after an overdone selloff.

breaking.headline: NATO Council meets today as Russian strikes kill 15 near Kyiv
breaking.fact: NATO's North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels today after Polish prosecutors confirmed all three objects that fell in southeastern Poland on Friday were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles; overnight Russian strikes killed at least 15 people across the Kyiv region, including an apartment-block hit in Dymer.

breaking.headline: Powerful Thanksgiving storm to hit East Coast Wednesday into the weekend
breaking.fact: The National Weather Service says confidence is high in a powerful coastal storm bringing heavy rain, high winds, snow and coastal impacts to the East Coast from Wednesday through Saturday, with 1–4 inches of rain, gusts over 50 mph on the coast and possible power outages and coastal flooding from Georgia to New England.

breaking.headline: Bahrain says Iranian strike wounded two, one critically
breaking.fact: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said Sunday that two people — a Bahraini citizen now stable and a Pakistani resident in critical condition — were wounded in Saturday's Iranian strike on a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island; Gulf states condemned the attack, and Secretary of State Rubio meets Qatar's prime minister in Washington today.

weekInBrief.headline: Asian governments move to halt the market rout
weekInBrief.body: South Korea readied a market stabilization fund and eased buybacks, Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission banned short sales below the prior close and raised short-sale margin to 150%, and Chinese exchanges eased margin rules for stock purchases, after Taiwan's market fell 17.5% last week — its worst week in 35 years — and the AI selloff spread across Asia.

weekInBrief.headline: Ukraine sinks a Russian warship off Libya
weekInBrief.body: Ukraine said Monday it sank the Russian corvette Merkury — one of the fleet's newest ships, commissioned in 2023 — with seven naval drones in the Libyan port of Benghazi on Sunday, destroying a Ka-27 helicopter aboard and also hitting the cargo vessel MV Angara, which Kyiv says Moscow used to move weapons; Libya's eastern government sought a UN investigation.

weekInBrief.headline: South Korea's exports top $1 trillion for the first time
weekInBrief.body: South Korea's cumulative 2026 exports passed $1 trillion on Nov. 19, making it only the fourth country ever to reach the mark and the first new member in 19 years, driven by semiconductors — $396.8 billion through October, nearly triple last year — and customs data Monday showed November exports still surging, up 101.5% in the first 20 days.

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin bounces 12% off a two-year low
weekInBrief.body: Bitcoin climbed to about $61,846 on Monday, up 12.3% from Saturday's two-year low near $55,000, as U.S. stock futures rebounded after last week's tech selloff; the token had slid below $60,000 last week as the AI rout spread to crypto.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Attacks on shipping in and around the strait are running at their highest level since the war began, CNN reports from UK Maritime Trade Operations data — more than 30 incidents in October and at least 22 so far in November — and projectiles struck three tankers leaving the strait over Friday and Saturday, setting fire to the Marshall Islands-flagged Captain Leon. President Trump dared Iran on Sunday to test the U.S. blockade, warning its vessels would end up “at the bottom of the sea,” and said he was inclined to resume U.S. strikes after the New Year if no deal is reached; U.S. Central Command warned last week that ships taking Iranian oil in ship-to-ship transfers can also be seized. On oil, Kpler reports Iranian oil on water outside the blockade zone has hit zero — no Iranian crude tanker has been confirmed to have escaped the blockade since July — while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11.

space.headline: Starship Flight 17 booster in full cryo testing; Flight 16 targeted for December
space.body: SpaceX's Flight 17 Super Heavy Booster (Booster 24) was venting liquid nitrogen in full cryogenic proof testing at Starbase on Sunday, while Ship 44 has finished its cryo tests; Flight 16 is targeted to launch in December, possibly from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, and the Flight 15 upper stage caught on Nov. 13 will go on public display rather than fly again.

space.headline: BepiColombo reaches Mercury after an eight-year journey
space.body: The ESA/JAXA BepiColombo spacecraft inserted itself into orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21 after eight years in space; its two probes — ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mio — will separate on Dec. 9–10, the first mission to fly two spacecraft around Mercury, with science operations set to begin in April 2027.

space.headline: Brain mapping reveals three stages of knowing your hand is yours
space.body: Karolinska Institutet researchers tracked brain activity millisecond by millisecond in 45 volunteers under the rubber-hand illusion and found the sense of body ownership unfolds in three distinct phases — starting before touch, then sweeping the right hemisphere, then engaging the left — a finding that may help explain body-perception problems after stroke.

space.headline: Ancient stone tools reveal a reuse pattern across southwest China
space.body: Archaeologists studying 166 scrapers and 58 resharpening flakes from 27 sites in southwest China found a Neanderthal-linked Quina toolmaking system — thick flakes repeatedly resharpened and reused, sometimes as a source of fresh cutting edges — that stretched across the region around 60,000–50,000 years ago.

apod.title: The Emergence of Dark Nebula Lynds 1251
apod.credit: David Cruz — Astronomy Picture of the Day
apod.explanation: If you stare into space for a long time, what might you see? At first, you might only see the usual brightest stars, but if your eyes (or camera) could continue to collect light, you would see increasingly more. In the direction of the featured image, after only a few minutes, you would begin to notice some regions without stars. As your staring continued, the dark region would become better defined, and after a full 20 hours, you would notice a strange dark structure. To celebrate, you use digital processing to brighten the image and enhance the colors. At the end, you might have an excellent image of Lynds 1251 (LDN 1251), a star-forming region laced with opaque brown-appearing interstellar dust. Also known as the Rotten Fish Nebula, LDN 1251 is home not only to young stars and dust, but also, your long staring indicates, energetic shock waves, fast stellar winds, and powerfully beamed jets.
